method: Measured the list-projection (names+desc+schema+caps, NO code) payload bytes + gpt-tokenizer count for cookbooks of N=4..500. Synthesized realistic entries (did not push 500 to prod — abusive). Real list-entry shape.
findings: Discovery cost grows LINEARLY: ~63 tokens per recipe in the list projection (code excluded).
At ~50 recipes (3K tokens) discovery is still cheap; at 200 (12.6K) it is heavy; at 500 (31.5K) the list ALONE is a context-firehose before the agent picks one.

This is the predicted 'matching, not storage' bottleneck: pantry stores fine at any scale, but a FLAT list does not scale for an AGENT to read and choose from. Past a few dozen recipes you need search/filter/ranking/embeddings, not a full list dump.
implication: Follow-on E6b: add a search/filter endpoint (GET /recipes?q= or capability/tag filter) so discovery cost is bounded by relevance, not cookbook size. The hub gets slower to USE as it gets more valuable to HAVE — unless discovery is indexed.
